sources.entry: ffWorks - Comprehensive Media Tool for macOS. Making High Quality Video Encoding Accessible for Everyone.

summary.name: ffWorks
summary.one_liner: ffWorks is a macOS graphical front end for FFmpeg that handles video and audio conversion, batch encoding, filters, subtitles and quality metrics through a visual interface.
use_cases: convert video files between formats on a Mac
batch encode many videos at once
compress video without losing much quality
burn or attach subtitles to video
create ProRes or HEVC encodes for production
measure video quality with VMAF or PSNR
summary.what_it_does: The app presents FFmpeg through drop zones: users create as many as they like and drop files onto one to process them to a chosen target. It offers colour adjustments (exposure, contrast, gamma, LUT presets), cropping with auto and black-border removal, and unlimited image or video overlays. Quality can be scored with VMAF, PSNR, SSIM and CAMBI, and tools show bitrate over time and generate thumbnail contact sheets. It also supports concatenating files, many codecs and containers, device and platform presets, and batches of up to 8 files at once, with Apple VideoToolBox for fast hardware encoding.
notable: Drop zones: unlimited configurable targets where dropped files are processed
Apple VideoToolBox hardware encoding for H264, H265 and ProRes
VMAF, PSNR, SSIM and CAMBI quality metrics plus bitrate analysis
Includes over 80 Pro LUT presets and many device presets
caveats: Requires an optional separately installed FFmpeg version for codec support
Priced at €22 per the page; it is a paid product
Batch processing is limited to 8 files simultaneously
